column1: # Why no phase owes each loud refusal that names none.
# crates/rexx-exec/src and requires a row here for each one that can build a message with
# no owner; it fails on such a constructor with no row, on a row whose constructor is gone,
# on a row for a constructor that names a phase (REHOME aside), and on a citation that does
# Columns, tab-separated: constructor, kind, phase, record.
#   GUARD      no program reaches it; the record names the probes that tried, or the
#              invariant that keeps it out of reach.
#   DEVIATION  matching the oracle is wrong; the record cites an oracle-crashes.txt entry, a
#   LIMIT      a design limit; the record cites the Deviation or design document licensing it.
#   REHOME     a remaining phase owes it; `phase` names it, the constructor carries it, and
#              the record quotes the roadmap row text naming the work.
# phase is `-` for every kind but REHOME.

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-phase-6-1-loose-ends.md section 4 (a wait only a command's peer can end is refused in sim): a command runs on the baton under a real-time bound, block= (2 s by default), and any command slower than it is refused, whether it waits on another activity or is only slow; timing-dependent by nature, and block= is how a program with slow commands runs under sim

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-phase-6-1-loose-ends.md section 4 (a wait only a native's own thread or a peer can end is refused in sim): a native call that leaves its driver runs on the baton under block=, past which the interpreter's thread is signalled once and the call refused once it returns; any such call slower than the bound is refused, timing-dependent by nature; a native that retries on EINTR or blocks outside a system call stays unbounded, and so does a native call under a pin, which does not leave its driver (it hangs on the oracle too)
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-phase-6-1-loose-ends.md section 4: a deadlock in the simulation mode is a loud refusal; virtual time cannot end a wait only a real signal can

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-phase-6-1-loose-ends.md section 4: any inbox post other than a signal's halt, and a callback from a thread running none of the interpreter's native calls, is a determinism breach, refused loudly

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-phase-6-1-loose-ends.md section 4 (trace and replay): a replay takes the trace's decisions in order, and one the run takes otherwise (another program, a damaged or edited file) is refused rather than run on a schedule the trace does not hold

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-phase-6-1-loose-ends.md section 4 (trace and replay): a run asked for a decision trace that it cannot write fails, so a harness that checks the status learns it has none
